correctness.rationale: All odd n>=11: opposite-pair circuits and opposite triples force 3f(0)=0. With that translation removed, a legal auxiliary t outside at most nine residues supplies three distinct-element triples forcing doubling; remaining non-distinct cases yield complete additivity. Thus the full group is exactly affine. The smooth geometric quotient follows from the prior labelled realization theorem and the degree-three embedding line bundle; generic stabilizer follows from the unique supporting cubic and ±1 automorphisms. A pure-standard-library exhaustive independent incidence check covers every odd n 11..33 and an explicit n=9 counterexample; it is not used as proof for all n.

originality.rationale: Borisov–Roulleau identify an included unit subgroup, and Baker proves the labelled modular realization scheme, neither of which gives the exact full automorphism group or the three-torsion kernel and consequently exhaustive unlabelled quotient. Search for equivalent zero-sum hypergraph groups and modular point-configuration quotients found no dominating statement; historical terminology risk is recorded, and the diamond quotient itself is acknowledged as classical.
residual_risks: A prior theorem on automorphism groups of zero-sum triple hypergraphs could be expressed under different terminology and imply the combinatorial result.

value.rationale: Full classification of combinatorial symmetries over infinitely many elliptic matroids identifies the *actual* unlabelled modular moduli curve, quantifies a three-torsion stabilizer transition and determines generic quotient degree. Nonaffine symmetries at n=9 show the n>=11 cutoff is not cosmetic. This supplies structural moduli information beyond known labelled realization results and beyond a routine case computation.
